mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals elevated labor market slack, which reduces wage growth and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% over two months signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL < 2% for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a fall in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over three months signals a precautionary savings shift, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises AND GDPC1 falls for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when this interaction is present.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in new single-family housing starts (HOUST) above 10% for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 10% monthly increase for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST rises by more than 10% for three consecutive months.
